items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: And along with oh, Benny Goodman and Count Basie, Duke Ellington.

ctx.x: Well, we’ve got some specific questions to ask about some of the big groups later on that you played with. Were you influenced by recordings?

Oh, yes. Like during the big band era I guess, the late ‘30’s and early ‘40’s and we always heard the big bands, you know, Tommy Dorsey was a good example of how the trombone ought to sound I guess. He was very popular. And along with oh, Benny Goodman and Count Basie, Duke Ellington. Trummy Young was, I remember that was one of the solos I used to practice on his solo in “Margie” when I was still in high school, with the Jimmy Lunceford band. He sang a chorus and then played a chorus. I think I never heard…
Did you ever have an occasion to play with Basie in any context?
